title: Any colour you pick for an arrow or measurement keeps its chip's words readable, Glass included
goal: A person can pick any colour at all for an arrow or a measurement, not only the palette, and every chip style keeps its words readable automatically, with no trip into Advanced. Glass, which lets the picture through, stays readable over a white screenshot and a black one alike.
notes: User, 2026-10-31 (intake): 'I want to make sure arrows/chips can be custom colored and it retains accessibility on the text, without going into advanced to tweak details'. Split out because the runner on caption-and-measurement-chips-come-in-a-set-of-p started at 13:25 and this direction was logged at 14:18; if that runner already did it, verify and close this as done. Reference implementation: docs/design/mocks/shared/components/markup.js (plateFor, glassFor), rules docs/design/markup.md section 3, live check on the design site: Design system > Markup, Custom colour well with a contrast readout.
acceptance: The Color row offers the palette plus a custom colour (the app's colour picker); picking any colour retints line, head and chip at once.

The plate rule in PhotonzCore matches docs/design/markup.md section 3 and window.PZ.markup.plateFor to the hex digit: a unit test sweeps every 5 degrees of hue x 4 saturations x 19 lightnesses (5,472 colours) over EVERY chip style and asserts words-to-plate contrast >= 4.5:1 (the design system measures 4.80 worst).

Glass derives its own tint (glassFor): at 82 percent opacity its words reach 4.8:1 over a pure white AND a pure black picture; white words on a darkened tint or dark words on a lightened one, whichever moves the colour less. Measured on a real white and a real black screenshot in the audit (before: a light ink on glass over white fell to 1.4:1).
A part overridden by hand under Advanced that drops a chip below 4.5:1 shows a short warning in the inspector, with a one-click way back to the automatic colour.
Walk: pick a custom light green and a custom indigo, check each chip style's words with the probe's pixel reader at 4.5:1 or better on light, dark and photo pictures.
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Done in caption-and-measurement-chips-come-in-a-set-of-p (2026-10-31): PhotonzCore InkPlate ports plateFor AND glassFor to the hex digit, held by ChipStyleTests against docs/design/markup-plate-sweep.tsv (5,472 colours written by Scripts/markup-plate-fixture.cjs from markup.js); the same sweep asserts every chip style >= 4.5:1 over white and black. The app DRAWS Glass at 95-97 percent (not 82) because its compositor blends in linear light (82 percent measured 3.2:1 over white); written into markup.md section 3. Hairline ink text now aims at 4.6 (byte rounding took 3 colours to 4.48), changed in markup.js too. captionLegibilityNote now warns under 4.5 (was 3). Still open here: the custom colour well in the Color row, one Color retinting the head as well as the chip (the chip already follows the line's ink), the one-click way back, and the walk.

Before building: a first-time user finds the colour on the arrow's Appearance (Chip, Color, Marker, per markup.md section 8) with no need to open the part rows; a Photoshop user expects swatches plus a well that opens a full picker, which is what the row is. The mock assumes a measurement chip with styles, which the app does not have yet: that is every-measurement-wears-the-same-chip-styles-col, so this task builds the arrow and that task got the row in its checklist.

Shipped in 91a9d770: Color row (MarkupInkRow, ChipStyleTiles.swift) with the design system's eight swatches and a Custom well (the app's picker); a pick goes through AnnotationContent.setInk (line, head unless painted apart, chip re-derived) in one undo step, and the tool bar colour on a picked arrow does the same. Warning 'Words are hard to read on this chip' + Reset Colors under the row (captionWordContrast judges the chip as drawn, see-through plates over white and black). Verified: ChipInkTests (5,472 colours x 10 styles, none under 4.5:1, no warning), ChipContrastReaderTests (light green and indigo, every style, white/black/photo, read off pixels), full Scripts/test.sh green, chip-styles-walk ok with the new row, audit queue/audits/2026-10-31-any-colour-chip-reads.json.
